HR Framework Library

Eight processes, five steps each, with the output that proves every step.

01Mandatory Benefits02Code Of Discipline03Hiring Process04Employee Retention05Performance Improvement Plan06Employee Portal07Birthday Wall08Performance Evaluation
Built on the Labor Code of the Philippines, DOLE department orders and related special laws. Contribution rates and agency circulars change — verify current issuances before applying.

One page per process, ready to post

Each framework runs left to right through five steps. The colored column is what to do; the card beneath it is the document the step must produce, so an audit trail builds itself as the work happens. The amber bar carries the compliance point most often missed.

The images are 2000 px PNGs sized for A4 landscape — drop them into a deck, print them, or pin them where the work is done.

Legal basisThe statute, article or department order each step answers to.
Five stepsThe official sequence, numbered in order of execution.
OutputThe record that proves the step was completed.
ComplianceThe failure point that turns a valid action into a violation.

01 / 08

Mandatory Benefits

Benefits every employer must give by law, no matter what company policy says. They cannot be waived, reduced or traded off. Unremitted contributions carry penalties, interest and personal liability for the responsible officers, while withdrawing a benefit already granted violates the non-diminution rule.

  • Labor Code of the Philippines (Arts. 86, 87, 94, 95, 100)
  • RA 11199 SSS
  • RA 11223 PhilHealth
  • RA 9679 Pag-IBIG
  • PD 851 13th Month Pay
  • PD 626 Employees Compensation
  • RA 7641 Retirement Pay
  • RA 11210, RA 8187, RA 11861, RA 9710, RA 9262 Leave Laws

ComplianceContribution rates, salary brackets and ceilings change by circular. Confirm the current SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG schedules and the BIR withholding table before every payroll run.

02 / 08

Code Of Discipline

A published table of offenses and penalties, plus the procedure for enforcing it. A rule can only be enforced if it is reasonable, made known to the employee beforehand and applied consistently. A valid cause is not enough on its own; procedural due process must also be observed.

  • Labor Code Arts. 297-299 [282-284] Just and Authorized Causes
  • DOLE Department Order No. 147-15
  • Omnibus Rules Implementing the Labor Code, Book V Rule XXIII (preventive suspension)
  • RA 7877 Anti-Sexual Harassment
  • RA 11313 Safe Spaces Act

ComplianceDismissal without the twin-notice procedure exposes the company to damages even when the cause is valid. Document the service and receipt of every notice.

03 / 08

Hiring Process

End-to-end recruitment that is fair, non-discriminatory and privacy-compliant, ending in a valid written contract with the standards communicated at the time of engagement. Selection must rest on job-related qualifications only, never on age, sex, civil status, pregnancy, religion, disability or health status.

  • Labor Code Art. 296 [281] Probationary Employment
  • RA 10911 Anti-Age Discrimination
  • RA 11261 First Time Jobseekers Assistance
  • RA 10173 Data Privacy Act
  • RA 7277 Magna Carta for Persons with Disability
  • RA 9710 Magna Carta of Women
  • RA 11166 (no HIV testing as a hiring condition)
  • RA 11058 OSH

ComplianceIf the regularization standards are not made known at the time of engagement, the employee is deemed regular from day one. Keep the signed standards form in the 201 file.

04 / 08

Employee Retention

A managed program to keep capable employees: correct pay, a safe and respectful workplace, growth, a real voice and wellbeing support. Retention is measured with data - turnover, tenure and exit reasons - not with impressions. Most avoidable resignations trace back to a compliance or supervision failure, not to salary alone.

  • Labor Code (wages, hours of work, rest days, security of tenure, Art. 100 non-diminution)
  • RA 11036 Mental Health Act & DOLE D.O. 208-20
  • RA 11058 & D.O. 198-18 Occupational Safety and Health
  • RA 11165 Telecommuting Act
  • D.O. 53-03 Drug-Free Workplace
  • D.O. 102-10 HIV/AIDS
  • D.O. 73-05 Tuberculosis
  • RA 11313 Safe Spaces Act

ComplianceRetention perks are voluntary, but a benefit given regularly and deliberately can ripen into company practice that cannot be unilaterally withdrawn (non-diminution rule, Art. 100).

05 / 08

Performance Improvement Plan

A time-bound, documented coaching program for an employee performing below standard. It is a corrective tool first, and most plans should end in recovery. It is also the evidence trail that makes any later separation defensible, because poor performance must be proven with records, not with opinion.

  • Labor Code Art. 296 [281] Probationary Standards
  • Art. 297 [282] (b) Gross and Habitual Neglect of Duties
  • DOLE Department Order No. 147-15
  • Settled jurisprudence on communicated standards, coaching and due process

ComplianceA PIP does not replace due process. Separation for poor performance still requires a Notice to Explain, an opportunity to be heard, and a written Decision citing the facts and grounds.

06 / 08

Employee Portal

One secure self-service system where employees view payslips, file leaves, read announcements and update their information. It cuts paper and repetitive HR queries, but it holds sensitive personal data, so privacy, access control and an audit trail are part of the build, not an afterthought.

  • RA 10173 Data Privacy Act & NPC Circular 16-01 (security of personal data)
  • RA 8792 E-Commerce Act (validity of electronic documents)
  • Labor Code Book III Rule X (payslips; records kept for three years)
  • BIR regulations on electronic payslips and Form 2316

CompliancePersonal data may be collected only for a declared purpose and kept no longer than necessary. Deactivate accounts on the separation date, not weeks later.

07 / 08

Birthday Wall

A simple recognition board that greets employees on their birthday and supports engagement at almost no cost. Because a birth date is personal information, it runs on voluntary opt-in consent and displays only the minimum, never the birth year or any contact detail. Participation and any contribution must always stay optional.

  • RA 10173 Data Privacy Act (consent, transparency, proportionality; a birth date is personal information)
  • RA 11313 Safe Spaces Act (respectful conduct in the workplace)
  • Company recognition and engagement policy

ComplianceA birthday wall is voluntary recognition, not a data collection exercise. Display the minimum, honor withdrawals at once, and never make celebration a condition of belonging.

08 / 08

Performance Evaluation

A regular, evidence-based review of results and behavior against standards communicated in advance. It drives pay, promotion and training decisions, and when performance falls short it becomes the record that supports coaching, a PIP or, ultimately, a valid separation. Ratings must rest on documented performance, never on personal characteristics.

  • Labor Code Art. 296 [281] Probationary Standards
  • Art. 297 [282] Just Causes
  • DOLE Department Order No. 147-15
  • RA 10911 Anti-Age Discrimination
  • RA 9710 Magna Carta of Women
  • RA 7277 Magna Carta for Persons with Disability
  • RA 11313 Safe Spaces Act

ComplianceA probationary employee not informed of the regularization standards at engagement becomes regular by operation of law, and one kept beyond six months becomes regular regardless of the rating.
